[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
Hugh Glasgow was born on 30 January 1710 and baptised on 5 February at Kilwinning, Ayrshire. The index names his parents as [[Glasgow-1927|John Glasgow]] and [[Gemill-4|Mary Gemmill]].<ref name="hughbirth">Findmypast, ''Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929'', [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3625904&tab=this Hugh Glasgow, 30 January/5 February 1710], Kilwinning, OPR 599/1, p. 70; FamilySearch [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYST-MFP record XYST-MFP].</ref>

A Kilmarnock marriage index records Hugh Glasgow and [[McEachin-120|Margaret McEachin]] on 20 March 1732.<ref name="marriage">FamilySearch, ''Scotland, Marriages, 1561–1910'', {{FamilySearch Record|XT24-XWR}}, Hugh Glasgow and Margaret McEachin, 20 March 1732. Original page not compared.</ref> Kilmarnock baptism indexes name Hugh and Margaret, whose surname appears as McEachan, McGlashan, McGechan or McCachen in different transcripts, for Mary (1732), Jean (1735), Margaret (1738), Hugh (1742), Ann (1749) and Hugh (1752). A 1755 Glasgow baptism names Hugh and Margtt. McKechny as parents of John. Each child's own profile holds its event-specific citation; the index spellings and child identifications should be compared against the original pages.<ref name="mary1732">Findmypast, Kilmarnock baptism [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3599128&tab=this Mary Glasgow, 17 December 1732], parents Hugh Glasgow and Margaret McGechan.</ref><ref name="john1755">FamilySearch, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VRS2-MNP John Glasgo, 19/23 April 1755], parents Hugh and Margtt. McKechny.</ref>

A separate Kilmarnock baptism dated 11 April 1744 names Hugh Glasgow and [[Giffen-664|Margaret Giffen]] as parents of another Mary. The source names a different mother and the same father name. This child event was retained from the former [[Glasgow-4166]] profile; its connection to the Kilwinning-born Hugh remains a qualified inference, not proof of a second marriage, widowhood or Margaret McEachin's death.<ref name="mary1744">Findmypast, Kilmarnock baptism [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3600620&tab=this Mary Glasgow, 11 April 1744], parents Hugh Glasgow and Margaret Giffen.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Father confidence review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1927]] is assessed at 93% (proved). The1710 Kilwinning transcript names John Glasgow and Mary Gemmill as Hugh’s parents, birth30January and baptism5February. John-1927 is the maintained Kilwinning father with this named couple and child sequence, supplying a specific adult-household match. The father’s own Linlithgow childhood and Hugh’s later Kilmarnock glover identification remain unbridged, so confidence is lower than an independently linked adult lifetime.

The record-defined1710 child and John/Mary household93%. This does not prove the1732–1742 Kilmarnock glover’s childhood or the Kilwinning John’s1671 Linlithgow identity. Original uninspected.

Next useful test: Use the glover’s marriage, trade and associated people to test the Kilwinning childhood; downstream baptisms alone cannot do so.

Source basis already held: [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3625904&tab=this Findmypast, Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564–1929, Hugh Glasgow, 30 January/5 February 1710 (https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3625904&tab=this), Kilwinning, OPR 599/1, p. 70; FamilySearch record XYST-MFP (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYST-MFP).]. No new original was inspected in this review. This is an assessment of an existing attachment, not a new father.


=== Kilmarnock glover household ===

The Kilmarnock baptism transcripts for Mary in 1732, Margaret in 1738 and Hugh in 1742 each name their father as Hugh Glasgow, a glover, resident at Kilmk (Kilmarnock). Repeated name, specific trade, locality and compatible child sequence identify one paternal household much more strongly than surname and chronology alone. The adult glover is represented by [[Glasgow-1929|Hugh Glasgow]]. Each of these three father–child roles is assessed separately at 99% subjective confidence. This concerns the recorded glover as father; his further identification with the 1710 Kilwinning child is an independent inferred step, not newly proved by these baptisms.

The retained transcripts actually give three maternal surname readings: McEachan for Mary in 1732, McGlashan for Margaret in 1738, and McGechan for Hugh in 1742. The 1732 marriage names Margaret McEachin. The same father, glover trade, parish and repeated Margaret given name support one family, but the McGlashan reading deserves separate treatment. The identification with [[McEachin-120|Margaret McEachin]] is assessed at 98% for Mary, 98% for Hugh and 84% for Margaret. McEachan and McGechan are compatible renderings in this specific household. McGlashan could be a transcription error or could distinguish another mother; the original entry is needed to resolve it.<ref>[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3599128&tab=this Findmypast retained transcript SCOT/OPR/BAP/3599128: Mary, 1732-12-17, OPR 597/1 item1 p.150; father Hugh Glasgow, glover; mother Margaret McEachan]. [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3599918&tab=this Findmypast retained transcript SCOT/OPR/BAP/3599918: Margaret, 1738-08-31, OPR 597/1 item1 p.206; father Hugh Glasgow, glover; mother Margaret McGlashan]. [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3600403&tab=this Findmypast retained transcript SCOT/OPR/BAP/3600403: Hugh, 1742-08-29, OPR 597/2 item2 p.20; father Hugh Glasgow, glover; mother Margaret McGechan]. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XT24-XWR FamilySearch XT24-XWR: Hugh Glasgow and Margaret McEachin, 20 March 1732, Kilmarnock; existing cited index, original uninspected].</ref>

The original register images have not been inspected. The 1744 Mary baptism naming Margaret Giffen remains a separate unresolved maternal comparison. These parental-role assessments do not establish the glover’s identification with the 1710 Kilwinning child.

The former Kilmarnock father profile Glasgow-4166 was merged into this one on 27 September 2026. The Kilwinning child of 1710 is age-compatible with the 1732 adult groom and father, and the 1732 marriage to Margaret McEachin together with recurring McGechan/McCachen forms in the Kilmarnock children provides a family bridge. The original Kilwinning and Kilmarnock records do not expressly identify the same Hugh, so the child-to-adult step remains inferred. Earlier profiles placed the first Hugh child with Margaret McEachin in 1749; the 1732–1742 Kilmarnock entries expand that sequence.

Two Mary baptisms, in 1732 and 1744, are separate records. They might be successive same-name children or belong to distinct same-name fathers. The 1744 Giffen entry should be examined separately for residence, occupation and witness details; preserve both recorded mothers and all child citations pending that comparison. No death date is established for Hugh.
